newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: MARADONA FACES NEW PATERNITY SUIT IN ARGENTINA.
newsitem.headline: MARADONA FACES NEW PATERNITY SUIT IN ARGENTINA.

text.p: Diego Maradona, the former soccer superstar from Argentina, was sued on Monday by a 20-year-old woman who claims he is the father of her baby.
"(She) tried several times to have Maradona admit his paternity, but he has systematically refused to do so," the woman's attorney, Dalila Pinacho, told reporters.

The woman, who filed suit in family court in Buenos Aires, said she expected the judge to order genetic tests within the next few days. Pinacho said the tests would prove Maradona was the father of the seven-month-old baby girl. The woman's identity was not revealed.
An Italian judged ruled four years ago that Maradona, who has seen glory and disgrace, was the father of a boy born in Naples in 1986, when he was playing for a local soccer team.
The 36-year-old player, who is married and has two young daughters, has refused to take genetic tests in that case.
Maradona's response to the latest paternity suit is not known. His lawyer was not immediately available for comment.
Maradona tasted fame early in his career, when in 1986 he was the star of Argentina's World Cup victory.

His success has been marred by repeated bouts with illegal drugs. In 1991 he was banned for 15 months for testing positive for cocaine while playing for Napoli, and in 1994 he was kicked out of the U.S. World Cup finals and banned from soccer for 15 months for failing a dope test.
Maradona's manager and best friend, Guillermo Coppola, is currently in jail on cocaine-dealing charges.
Maradona, who has admitted to his cocaine addiction and been under treatment several times, has left and returned to professional soccer several times.
The former star has not played for his club Boca Juniors for more than three months and two weeks ago, after a rare training session, he said: "I haven't got the strength" and quit again.
